programme.title: An Là

programme.title: Fonn mo Bheatha
programme.desc: Ceòl agus còmhradh le Cathy Ann Nic a Phi còmhla ri Mairi Mac a Ghobhainn Archive Music and chat programme presented by Cathy Ann MacPhee with guest Mary Smith. Producer:- Magaidh NicFhionghuin In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Mas Fhior
programme.desc: Niall Iain Macdonald hosts a new quiz show where more than general knowledge is required to win. Standing in the way of our two teams from winning are the Pretenders, who, from the comfort of their own homes, are on a mission to fox our contestants. Which of this week’s teams, Marcas and Morvyn or Fraoch and Raibeart, will get the upper hand and have a chance to take home the grand prize? Niall Iain Dòmhnallach le farpais cheist ùr far a bheil barrachd air eòlas coitcheann a dhìth gus buannachadh. Tha na Mas Fhìoraich a’ gabhail pàirt bhon dachaighean ’s ag amas air a’ chùis a dhèanamh air an dà sgioba. Cò aca bho sgiobaidhean na seachdain-sa, Marcas & Morvyn no Fraoch & Raibeart, a gheibh làmh an uachdar agus cothrom fhaighinn air an duais mhòr? In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Garradh Phadruig
programme.desc: It’s late summer but Peter still has work to do and vegetables to harvest. Deireadh samhraidh ach tha obair aig Pàdruig ri dhèanamh agus glasraich ri bhuain.

programme.title: Rùm Gu Rùm, Le Erica
programme.desc: Tha an cleasaiche, a tha a-nis na dealbhaiche cruthachail thaighean, Erica Mhoireasdan, a’ gabhail sgrìob tron Ghàidhealtachd ‘s na h-Eileanan. Le taic bho luchd-ciùird, tha i a’ lorg dhòighean ùra air seann rumanan a thoirt beò. Actress turned interior designer Erica Morrison takes us on a design adventure throughout the Highlands and Islands. With the help of local craft workers, she finds new ideas for designing old spaces. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Valtos | Aig a’ Mhullach
programme.desc: Ceòl dannsa aig mullach a’ Chùirn Ghuirm, le na DJs Gàidhealach Valtos a’ toirt an cuid chiùil gu ìre eile le seata ciùil slàn, High Water Mark. Ceòl gun sgur bhon ùrlar-dannsaidh as àirde ann an Alba. Thig cuide ri Martyn, Dan agus Euan is iad a’ dèanamh ùrlar-dannsaidh à Stèisean Tàrmagain. Le ceòl bho Bicep, Charles J, Le Boom, Mylo, Oliver Heldens am measg eile, is cuideachd, Valtos fhèin. Dance floor fillers on top of Cairngorms as Highland DJs Valtos present High Water Mark, taking their music to new heights. In a pure, uninterrupted DJ set, join Martyn, Dan and Euan as they transform the iconic Ptarmigan Station into the highest dance floor in Scotland. Featuring tracks from Bicep, Charles J, Le Boom, Mylo and Oliver Heldens, as well as Valtos. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Runrig - The Last Dance
programme.desc: 50,000 neach-leantainn a’ dèanamh air Sruighlea gus ciurm-ciùil slàn Runrig 2018 fhaicinn, a’ comharrachadh deireadh cùrsa-beatha soirbheachail 45-bliadhna. 50,000 fans descend on Stirling to watch much-loved Scottish rock band Runrig’s 2018 poignant farewell concert, marking the end of a successful 45-year career.

programme.title: Tuath Cheòl le Ruairidh Gray
programme.desc: An seinneadair Ruairidh Gray a’ tadhal air an Grand Ole Opry ann an Glaschu agus a’ toirt sùil air ais air sreathan Tuath Cheòl. Bidh Ruairidh a’ taghadh cuid de na taisbeanaidhean a bha anns na prògraman agus a bha a’ còrdadh gu mòr ri luchd-leantainn ceòl dùthchasach aig an àm. Am measg na bhios anns a’ phrògram seo, Anna Latharna NicIllÌosa, Cathy Anna Nic a Phì, Tom Sloss nach maireann agus à Ceap Breatainn, Natalie McMaster agus Tracey Dares. Singer Ruairidh Gray visits Glasgow’s Grand Ole Opry for a look back at the legendary music series Tuath Cheòl and presents musical selections from the original programmes. Hugely popular with country music fans at the time, this episode features musicians and singers including Anne Lorne Gillies, Cathy Anne MacPhee, the late Tom Sloss and, from Cape Breton, Natalie McMaster and Tracey Dares. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Life on Earth
programme.desc: The story of life, from the first primitive cells to the plants and animals that now live around us. David Attenborough examines the uses and advantages of birds' unique possession - the feather. Man has yet to invent anything that, weight for weight, is as strong as the feather. programme.title: Gloria Hunniford Remembers... Doris Day
programme.desc: In the 1950s and 60s, Doris Day ranked amongst cinema’s biggest box office stars, thanks to roles in films such as musical Calamity Jane, Hitchcock’s The Man Who Knew Too Much, and especially a string of hit romantic comedies, including the classic Pillow Talk. Amongst the movie icon’s millions of fans across the world was a young Gloria Hunniford, who in 1995, years after Doris had unexpectedly stepped back from Hollywood and swapped fame for anonymity, was invited to Doris’s home in Carmel, USA, for an exclusive opportunity to interview her heroine. Here, ahead of a special screening of that rare interview, Gloria draws back the curtain on her encounter with one of cinema’s great female idols and shares her memories of how the meeting came together, and the special behind-the-scenes moments that TV viewers of the day never got to see.

programme.title: Clive Myrie’s Caribbean Adventure
programme.desc: Clive heads to one of the Dominican Republic’s most northerly provinces, to the beautiful city of Puerto Plata. He learns about the incredible story of the Jewish refugees that found shelter in this country during World War II. He also discovers how to make the delicious plantain dish of mofongo, meets some of the finest merengue musicians in the country and heads to a busy banana farm, where he discovers a Dominican drink with a very racy reputation.

programme.title: The Big Cases
programme.desc: The chilling story of Hull’s funeral home horror. How an undertaker drowning in debt betrayed hundreds of grieving families. Robert Bush hoarded bodies, sold fake funeral plans and presented families with the ashes of strangers. His shocking crimes went undetected for years. The discovery led to one of the most complex investigations in Humberside Police’s history, with help from the National Crime Agency. At the heart of this are grieving families. In their darkest days, they fought for laws to regulate the funeral industry so that others never suffer their pain - or guilt - again.

programme.title: The Climate Question
programme.desc: A global programme that reflects the variety of takes on climate change, how best to understand it and the world's attempts to avert it, temper it or adapt to it. It is not about questioning whether climate change is happening, it's about finding the best ways to respond to it. This is sharp-edged, analytical inquiry. Hard scrutiny, touched with a sense of adventure and discovery, and where we can find it, hope. It includes stories from across the world on why we find it so hard to save our own planet, and how we might change that.

programme.title: The Travel Show
programme.desc: The traditional French bistro is mounting a comeback. In recent times, an average of 25 a day have been shutting their doors, as eating habits change across France. Now though, efforts are underway to save them. Briony May Williams travels through the south of the country to find out what this casual form of dining has brought to French culture. She heads to a village that's finally about to reopen a bistro that it lost many years ago, and explores the rowdy breakfast culture of Lyon's Machon cafes.

programme.title: Talking Business
programme.desc: Can oil really save Venezuela’s economy? The country has the world’s largest reserves, so can it take advantage whilst global energy supplies are under pressure because of events in the Middle East? Reviving Venezuela’s biggest industry is just one part of the change that’s needed as the country recovers from deadly earthquakes and tries to restructure a mountain of debt after years of mismanagement. Respected former central bank president Ruth Krivoy and leading oil executive Ali Moshiri of Amos Global Energy give their takes on the role oil can play. Meanwhile, the president of Venezuela’s Chambers of Commerce and Industry, Felipe Capozzolo of Fedecamaras, explains some of the other reforms that could help the country become wealthy again.

They could be anything from famous faces, places, products or logos, and teams need to name them all for a Picture Slam. Playing this time are friends Samantha and Shane from Coventry, siblings Taran and Raj from London and father and son Adam and Oliver from Glasgow. They battle it out across four rounds, shouting out answers and building their banks. But only one team can make it to the final Super Slam for the chance to win £10,000.

programme.title: Michael McIntyre's Big Show
programme.desc: BAFTA award-winning comedian Michael McIntyre hosts his Big Show, an unmissable night of family entertainment broadcast from London's prestigious Theatre Royal Drury Lane. Comedian Josh Widdicombe is woken up for a hilarious edition of the Midnight Gameshow. Boxing star Tony Bellew hands over his phone in Send to All. The Darkness frontman Justin Hawkins gets the shock of his life in the Unexpected Star Star of the Show, and Olly Alexander performs.

programme.title: Pointless Celebrities
programme.desc: A celebrity special edition of the general knowledge quiz in which four teams try to come up with the answers that no-one else could think of. Presented by Alexander Armstrong and co-host Richard Osman. Featuring Charlene White, Fern Britton, Chloe Madeley, James Haskell, Crystelle Pereira, Kwoklyn Wan, Phil Wang and Pierre Novellie.

programme.title: How Are You? It's Alan (Partridge)
programme.desc: Newly single and never happier, Alan throws himself into new experiences to see if trying fresh things can improve our wellbeing - and finds joy in the unexpected.

programme.title: BBC Weekend News
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: BBC Weather
programme.desc: The latest weather forecast.

programme.title: Bridget Jones's Diary
programme.desc: Romantic comedy telling the story of a neurotic thirty-something who resolves to take control of her life once and for all. She drinks, smokes and eats too much, and, worst of all, she falls for the wrong kind of man - passing over Mr Right for Mr Right Now. From the novel by Helen Fielding.

programme.title: Man Up
programme.desc: Nancy, 34 years old and single, is travelling across London to toast another ten years of her parents' magical marriage. She runs into 40-year-old divorcee Jack, who mistakes her for his blind date. Nancy decides to go with it and starts the most chaotic journey of her life. A romantic comedy about taking chances, making decisions and rolling with the consequences.

programme.title: Breakfast
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, business and weather from the BBC's Breakfast team.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt brings an array of delicious recipes from Paul Ainsworth, Judy Joo and Donal Skehan. And we head out of the studio with Rick Stein and the Hairy Bikers.

programme.title: Anna Haugh’s Big Irish Food Tour
programme.desc: In her teenage years, TV presenter and Wicklow native Laura Whitmore was fond of Ireland's famous chicken fillet rolls. Nowadays Laura is more mindful of what she eats and wants to show Anna the great produce available on the Wicklow coast. Anna meets a farming family who have been recognised internationally for their award-winning cheeses. The two visit Airfield Estate urban farm with gardening gloves at the ready as they get a lesson in growing their own vegetables.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A developer in Plymouth has tunnel vision with his plans to dig down at a bungalow, Martin is cracking up at a semi-detached house in Staffordshire, and in Suffolk, Jacqui sees the potential in a detached property.

programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.desc: The latest weather forecast.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles challenges the people of Lincolnshire on their antiques knowledge. Can they guess his mystery item? It’s from the 19th century. It can be made of pewter or tin. It has a pumping action and an ever so tedious link to Lincolnshire history. Over at Hemswell antiques centre, the reds and blues are pumped up as they go head to head to see who can buy the best items to sell at auction. Up the road at North Hykeham is where they hope to make some profits - guided by auctioneer Colin Young. Expert Catherine Southon is leading the reds, and expert Mark Stacey is with the blues.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Restorer Peter falls in love with a rosewood coffee table, and upcycling sisters Katie and Sophie have a fabric mishap.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Looking for a new adventure in south west Wales, today’s couple have £400,000 to find a new home with at least an acre of land for glamping and a forestry school. Ginny Buckley helps with the house hunting and meets another couple who, ten years ago, made a life-changing escape when they bought a farm in Carmarthenshire to rear rare breeds.

programme.title: Night at the Museum: Secret of the Tomb
programme.desc: 'Life' for the New York exhibits will end unless Larry gets the decaying mystic tablet to the British Museum for advice from Ahkmenrah’s pharoah father. The desperate quest soon involves Sir Lancelot and stroppy night guard Tilly. Third of the action comedy films.

programme.title: Reporting Scotland
programme.desc: All the weekend national, UK-wide and international news on Saturday evening at 7.

programme.title: Icons of Football
programme.desc: When your nickname is Jaws, your reputation goes before you. Joe Jordan struck fear into opposing defenders with his full-blooded approach to football. Graduating with flying colours from the school of hard knocks at Elland Road in the 1970s, where he won a league title, Joe starred for Manchester United, before leaving a tangible legacy with Italian giants AC Milan. However, his performances and goals for Scotland on the biggest of stages are what have cemented him as an icon of the game. The only Scottish player to have scored in three World Cups, Joe sits comfortably among the elite of the game. He reveals how he made the most of the ability he had to forge a top-class career in the game, and how the grounding he got in the intense Leeds dressing room would help shape the career of future footballing greats such as Franco Baresi and Mauro Tassotti. Joe also reflects on the lifelong friendship he made with the late, great Gordon McQueen, and how McQueen’s death from dementia has made him reflect on a career heading footballs. Featuring contributions from Fabio Capello, Mauro Tassotti, John Giles, Hayley McQueen and Graham Hunter.

programme.title: Sportscene: Premiership Highlights
programme.desc: Highlights of Dundee v Aberdeen and St Mirren v St Johnstone.

programme.title: Loch Ness
programme.desc: An American scientist meets hostility from loch locals as he tries to prove the existence of the Loch Ness monster.

programme.title: From Scotland with Love
programme.desc: Made entirely of Scottish film archive, a journey into our collective past, the film explores universal themes of love, loss, resistance, migration, work and play. Ordinary people, some long since dead, their names and identities largely forgotten, appear shimmering from the depths of the vaults to take a starring role. These silent individuals become composite characters, who emerge to tell us their stories, given voice by King Creosote's poetic music and lyrics.

programme.title: Hercules the Bear - A Love Story
programme.desc: The remarkable true story of the world’s most famous grizzly bear and the Scottish couple who raised him as their own. In 1975, wrestler Andy Robin and his wife, Maggie, adopted nine-month-old bear cub Hercules and set out to tame one of the world’s fiercest animals. What followed was an extraordinary tale of wrestling, rescue and super stardom. Featuring never-seen-before home video, this heartwarming film revisits the incredible bond between Andy, Maggie and Hercules the bear.

programme.title: Loop
programme.desc: Birmingham-born, Glasgow-based author Maisie Chan shares her unique, personal story to becoming a successful children’s author. Passionate about creating better Asian representation in literature, Maisie wrote her first book, Danny Chung Does Not Do Maths, which became shortlisted for the 2020 Blue Peter Book Award. Now, as Maisie prepares to launch her second novel, Loop meets Maisie and learns how her role as a young carer to her adoptive parents has shaped the narrative in her new novel, Keeping Dancing, Lizzie Chu.

programme.desc: Puss in Boots gets his own animated adventure film in this Shrek spin-off. Puss teams up with a fellow thieving feline and his old friend Humpty Dumpty to embark on an exciting quest. The trio plan to find magic beans in order to steal the goose that lays the golden eggs, but all does not go according to plan. Featuring the voices of Antonio Banderas (Puss), Salma Hayek (Kitty Softpaws), Zach Galifianakis (Humpty Alexander Dumpty), Billy Bob Thornton (Jack), Amy Sedaris (Jill), Constance Marie (Imelda), Guillermo Del Toro (Moustache Man/Commandante) and Mike Mitchell (Andy Beanstalk).

programme.title: Not Going Out
programme.desc: When Lee goes to watch Benji playing football for a local under-13 team, he is unable to restrain himself on the touchline and becomes the competitive dad that all other parents want to avoid. Undaunted by the disapproval of Toby, who coaches the team, Lee sets about rigging the vote for the player of the year.

programme.title: Not Going Out
programme.desc: Lucy has cooked a special meal so that she and Lee can spend an evening in without distractions to talk about the state of their marriage. But Lee is obsessed with a beeping noise in the house that he can’t find, and the food is soon forgotten.

programme.title: Not Going Out
programme.desc: It’s Lucy's birthday. To celebrate, Geoffrey and Wendy take Lee, Lucy, Toby and Anna for a trip on a vintage steam train. But Lee's decision to play Poirot when a stranger turns up unannounced in their carriage risks Lucy’s special day being ruined.

programme.title: Mrs Brown's Boys
programme.desc: Agnes Brown's grandson Bono is being bullied by a boy at school. When Agnes makes matters worse, a mediation session is called.

programme.title: Mrs Brown's Boys
programme.desc: When a crime wave hits Finglas, the garda prompts Father Damien and Maria to put together a neighbourhood watch scheme. Agnes and Winnie promptly sign up, but are they really the best people to tackle crime in the area? After Cathy goes on yet another disastrous date, Agnes is determined to put Cathy's man troubles to rest once and for all. Although when they say it's good to 'air your problems', they probably don't mean literally. Meanwhile, Betty and Mark lock horns over whether Bono should go to his school disco.

programme.title: Ghosts Australia
programme.desc: The Australian version of the hit UK series. When city couple Kate and Sean inherit Ramshead Manor, a run-down country estate, they see it as a sign for a fresh new start. But after Kate has a near-death experience, she gains the ability to see and hear ghosts – and discovers there are several living in the mansion. Kate must navigate the ghosts' issues while trying to start a hotel business with Sean, who remains unable to see them.

David’s boss saddles him with his biggest responsibility yet: her 14-year-old stepdaughter.

programme.title: Schitt's Creek
programme.desc: After Moira experiences a sleepless night due to a noisy next-door neighbour, Johnny is surprised to discover who the culprit is. Now Johnny and Moira must find a way to bring peace back to their motel home. With money from her new job, Alexis goes apartment-hunting with David.

programme.title: Schitt's Creek
programme.desc: When some of Moira’s campaign signs mysteriously disappear, Johnny immediately accuses Roland of foul play. David suddenly finds himself unemployed when the Blouse Barn becomes entangled in a legal dispute. With the help of Alexis, David tries to turn the situation into a financial windfall for his boss.

programme.title: Ideal
programme.desc: Sitcom about a small-time dope dealer and his strange collection of acquaintances. The police constable has fallen in love with China, Nicki thinks she's losing her mind, Brian has turned into a goth, and Moz is forced to perform an exorcism on Jenny the gormless child minder.

programme.title: Ideal
programme.desc: Sitcom about a small-time dope dealer and his strange collection of acquaintances. Moz is desperate to dissuade Cartoon Head and Psycho Paul from shooting a porn film in his bathroom. programme.title: Ideal
programme.desc: Sitcom about a small-time dope dealer and his strange collection of acquaintances. Moz receives an unwelcome visit from terrifying gang leader Stemroach. The discovery of a wasps' nest in the loft has disastrous consequences for the born-again Christian builders.

programme.title: BBC Comedy Short Films
programme.desc: Calamity James is a slapstick comedy about a young man, James, who is cursed with ‘acute misfortune syndrome’. In this world, chronic bad luck exists and the unbelievable is the everyday.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: When running a big school, how much discipline is too much? Panorama investigates the academy trust where classrooms are silent and pupils can be sent to detention for looking out of the window. For some, reduced disruption and improved exam results at schools run by the Athena Learning Trust in Devon and Cornwall is proof that the tough approach works. But as Richard Bilton reports, many former teachers, students and their parents say the trust’s strict policies on behaviour have gone too far.

programme.title: The Rapture
programme.desc: Gabs and Dick uncover evidence that Leonard is hiding something, while floods in India match Bethany’s drawings. Gabs pushes her suspicions into the open.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: Brinicle tries to turn the Krispy Krill shack into a top restaurant to impress a secret reviewer, but chef Pancake’s cooking proves unpopular, and Looph’s plate machine misfires.

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: Whilst playing doctors, Cosima discovers an animal with no heartbeat! Can Cosima and Big Lizard save the poor creature with Dad's medical kit?

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: The ducklings get creative and make sculptures of themselves out of straw. Weasy thinks he can do better, but his sculpture is a fiasco. The Farm of the Future offers a precise cutting system. Will Weasy be able to outsmart his daughters?

programme.title: Super Happy Magic Forest
programme.desc: Blossom draws the short cheese straw and, rather than join her friends on a picnic, she has to take a magic wand to the recycling centre. Faced with a long queue and a rumbly tummy, Blossom decides that life is too short for recycling - with disastrous consequences. The heroes must skip their picnic and go on a quest to save the forest from the magical mess Blossom has gotten them into.

programme.title: Grizzy and the Lemmings
programme.desc: Grizzy finds a polar bear and realises they are from the same species.

programme.title: Duck and Frog
programme.desc: When Duck and Frog work on a farm, Frog makes the perfect scarecrow. However, he gets covered in super-strong fertiliser and becomes a giant, monster-sized, chaos-causing Frog!

programme.title: Pokémon Horizons
programme.desc: Amethio meets Mighty G, and a surfing Gholdengo wows the Rising Volt Tacklers.

programme.title: Winx Club - The Magic Is Back
programme.desc: A dark spell transforms Bloom into Dark Bloom, turning her against her friends and wreaking havoc at Alfea. Meanwhile, Aisha's love of dance clashes with her parents' expectations.

programme.title: The Next Step: Cheer
programme.desc: When a legendary coach abruptly leaves a highly successful cheerleading gym, the team are left in disarray, The Next Step’s Kenzie steps in to take over what’s left of the team, desperate to prove she is more than just a dancer, and that she can build this rag-tag group of athletes into a contender for nationals.

programme.title: Newsround
programme.desc: Topical news magazine for children.

programme.title: Jamie Johnson FC
programme.desc: It’s all change at Hawx Academy as former Foxborough player Charlie must prove herself to her teammates, their new coach and an all-access documentary crew.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Frances Tophill returns to Damson Farm in Bath and spends the day with owner Alison and a very special guest – Dame Mary Berry. Returning to the city where she grew up and went to school, Mary shares how the landscapes and countryside around Bath nurtured a lifelong love of gardening and the great outdoors. Together, they share practical gardening advice and celebrate the very best of summer, harvesting homegrown fruit, vegetables and flowers at their seasonal peak. Frances has advice on how to create a wild corner that's both beautiful and beneficial for wildlife while collecting seeds for future displays. Arit Anderson visits an inspiring urban edible garden in London, and there's a city gardener transforming a compact space into a thriving haven for wildlife. Toby Buckland shares clever ways to extend the growing season and make the most of summer harvests, and in Birmingham, there's a visit to a predominantly Punjabi allotment community where growing exceptional produce is intertwined with family, culture and tradition, creating plots that are as productive as they are beautiful.

programme.title: Angels One Five
programme.desc: Second World War drama relating the Battle of Britain through the eyes of the operations room of a Kent fighter station during the summer of 1940. A young, inexperienced pilot has trouble settling into the routine of squadron life, and his adherence to the rule book puts him out of favour with his comrades. Can he win them round?

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: The ten remaining sewers celebrate the rich fashion and textile traditions of Mexico. Host Sophie Willan and judges Patrick Grant and Esme Young are joined by a special guest judge, renowned fashion designer Erika Alvirez. In the Pattern Challenge, the sewers create a Mexican folkloric top using fabrics created by indigenous communities in Mexico’s Oaxaca region. For the Transformation Challenge, they are given manteles de hule, a traditional Mexican tablecloth. Using the stiffness of the fabric, they are asked to create a garment with an eye-catching structure. Finally, in the Made-to-Measure, the sewers design an outfit inspired by one of the many Mexican festivals found across the country.

programme.title: A Cook Abroad
programme.desc: MasterChef judge Monica Galetti steps outside her comfort zone as she swaps her chef's whites for wellies and heads for the Jura Mountains in eastern France to get hands-on with the produce she uses every day in the London restaurant where she works. Monica embarks on a road trip through one of the most beautiful yet least known regions in France, where, for the first time in her cooking career, she spends time with producers. She sees for herself how their passion translates into world-class ingredients. Immersing herself in a traditional way of life, she joins a boar hunt and faces up to the responsibility of eating meat. From beauty contests for cows to cutting down trees, she unlocks the secret to making some of our favourite French cheeses and discovers an ancient profession she never knew existed. Finally, on the slopes of Mont d'Or, Monica cooks up a rustic feast using ingredients she's gathered herself, fulfilling a personal ambition to live off the land.

programme.title: Summer Holiday
programme.desc: Don and his friends persuade their employer to lend them a London bus for their summer holiday. En route to the south of France, the boys run into some girls and offer them a lift to Athens. Then, they pick up an American boy who isn't exactly what he seems but who is running away from an exploitative mother.

programme.title: Fake or Fortune?
programme.desc: Our art sleuths investigate 15 prints found in a garage, each potentially worth thousands. Are they really by notorious 20th-century artist Lucian Freud? Or just crafty fakes?

programme.title: Evolution
programme.desc: How did the dolphin get so smart? Chris Packham dives into one of the biggest questions in nature - how intelligence itself evolved and how it arose in the extraordinary mind of the dolphin. Inside each one lies the result of a three-billion-year journey, from light-sensing cells to conscious thought.

programme.title: Superman II
programme.desc: Three Kryptonian criminals who share Superman’s extraordinary powers arrive on Earth with the intent of conquering it. Superman must use all his strength and intelligence to outwit them.

programme.title: BBC Proms
programme.desc: Nick Mohammed journeys through the Proms archive to celebrate the music that transformed people's view of the universe. Featuring Richard Strauss's Also sprach Zarathustra from 2001: A Space Odyssey, Gustav Holst's The Planets, John Williams's scores for Star Wars and E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, Hans Zimmer's Interstellar and Max Richter's On the Nature of Daylight, heard in Arrival. Prepare for a journey from the concert hall to galaxies far, far away.

programme.title: Paul Heaton at the BBC
programme.desc: One of Britain’s most prolific and successful singer-songwriters of the past four decades, Paul Heaton started his career as frontman of The Housemartins before forming The Beautiful South, the band of whom it was famously once claimed that one in seven UK households owns an album. Whether that's true or not, what is a fact is that Paul has demonstrated over the years a unique ability to write songs and lyrics that have fans weeping one moment and smiling the next. This collection of performances and best BBC moments celebrates Paul’s impressive career - the bands, the collaborations and the solo work - and features the man himself explaining the context and backstories behind some of his best-loved hits. From The Housemartins’ debut release Sheep through to Fish 'N' Chip Supper from his solo album The Mighty Several and a triumphant appearance at Glastonbury 2024 that featured a glorious reunion with Norman ‘Fatboy Slim’ Cook, it’s a celebration that can definitely guarantee viewers a Happy Hour (and a half).

programme.title: Paul Heaton: Live at Bramall Lane
programme.desc: Paul Heaton takes to the stage at Sheffield's iconic Bramall Lane for a landmark concert. Recorded live in 2025, this unforgettable performance showcases one of Britain's most admired songwriters with songs spanning more than four decades, from the timeless classics of The Housemartins and The Beautiful South to highlights from his solo career. Backed by his stellar live band, including regular singing partner Rianne Downey, Paul Heaton delivers a set filled with wit, warmth and unmistakable melodies, performing beloved favourites alongside newer material for an audience at his beloved Sheffield United Football Club.

programme.title: The Housemartins in London 0 Hull 4
programme.desc: The Housemartins wake up one morning to discover that suddenly they're the fourth-best band in Hull. This intimate documentary is a unique record of the early days, looking at how a meteoric rise to fame left their home lives irrevocably unchanged. First broadcast 1987.

programme.title: Top of the Pops
programme.desc: A compilation of Top of the Pops performances from The Beautiful South.

programme.title: Fallen Leaves
programme.desc: Comedy romance set in modern-day Helsinki. A lonely metalworker and a single woman working as a supermarket shelf stacker meet by chance in a karaoke bar. Drawn to each other, they strike a quiet yet immediate connection. Along their uneven path to happiness lie lost phone numbers, mistaken addresses, alcoholism and a charming stray dog. Aki Kaurismäki's Nordic comedy romance, winner of the Cannes Festival Jury Prize. In Finnish with English subtitles.

Drawn to each other, they strike a quiet yet immediate connection. Along their uneven path to happiness lie lost phone numbers, mistaken addresses, alcoholism and a charming stray dog. Aki Kaurismäki's Nordic comedy romance, winner of the Cannes Festival Jury Prize. In Finnish with English subtitles.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: When running a big school, how much discipline is too much? Panorama investigates the academy trust where classrooms are silent and pupils can be sent to detention for looking out of the window. For some, reduced disruption and improved exam results at schools run by the Athena Learning Trust in Devon and Cornwall is proof that the tough approach works. But as Richard Bilton reports, many former teachers, students and their parents say the trust’s strict policies on behaviour have gone too far.

programme.title: The Rapture
programme.desc: Gabs and Dick uncover evidence that Leonard is hiding something, while floods in India match Bethany’s drawings. Gabs pushes her suspicions into the open.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: Brinicle tries to turn the Krispy Krill shack into a top restaurant to impress a secret reviewer, but chef Pancake’s cooking proves unpopular, and Looph’s plate machine misfires.

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: Whilst playing doctors, Cosima discovers an animal with no heartbeat! Can Cosima and Big Lizard save the poor creature with Dad's medical kit?

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: The ducklings get creative and make sculptures of themselves out of straw. Weasy thinks he can do better, but his sculpture is a fiasco. The Farm of the Future offers a precise cutting system. Will Weasy be able to outsmart his daughters?

programme.title: Super Happy Magic Forest
programme.desc: Blossom draws the short cheese straw and, rather than join her friends on a picnic, she has to take a magic wand to the recycling centre. Faced with a long queue and a rumbly tummy, Blossom decides that life is too short for recycling - with disastrous consequences. The heroes must skip their picnic and go on a quest to save the forest from the magical mess Blossom has gotten them into.

programme.title: Grizzy and the Lemmings
programme.desc: Grizzy finds a polar bear and realises they are from the same species.

programme.title: Duck and Frog
programme.desc: When Duck and Frog work on a farm, Frog makes the perfect scarecrow. However, he gets covered in super-strong fertiliser and becomes a giant, monster-sized, chaos-causing Frog!

programme.title: Pokémon Horizons
programme.desc: Amethio meets Mighty G, and a surfing Gholdengo wows the Rising Volt Tacklers.

programme.title: Winx Club - The Magic Is Back
programme.desc: A dark spell transforms Bloom into Dark Bloom, turning her against her friends and wreaking havoc at Alfea. Meanwhile, Aisha's love of dance clashes with her parents' expectations.

programme.title: The Next Step: Cheer
programme.desc: When a legendary coach abruptly leaves a highly successful cheerleading gym, the team are left in disarray, The Next Step’s Kenzie steps in to take over what’s left of the team, desperate to prove she is more than just a dancer, and that she can build this rag-tag group of athletes into a contender for nationals.

programme.title: Newsround
programme.desc: Topical news magazine for children.

programme.title: Jamie Johnson FC
programme.desc: It’s all change at Hawx Academy as former Foxborough player Charlie must prove herself to her teammates, their new coach and an all-access documentary crew.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Frances Tophill returns to Damson Farm in Bath and spends the day with owner Alison and a very special guest – Dame Mary Berry. Returning to the city where she grew up and went to school, Mary shares how the landscapes and countryside around Bath nurtured a lifelong love of gardening and the great outdoors. Together, they share practical gardening advice and celebrate the very best of summer, harvesting homegrown fruit, vegetables and flowers at their seasonal peak. Frances has advice on how to create a wild corner that's both beautiful and beneficial for wildlife while collecting seeds for future displays. Arit Anderson visits an inspiring urban edible garden in London, and there's a city gardener transforming a compact space into a thriving haven for wildlife. Toby Buckland shares clever ways to extend the growing season and make the most of summer harvests, and in Birmingham, there's a visit to a predominantly Punjabi allotment community where growing exceptional produce is intertwined with family, culture and tradition, creating plots that are as productive as they are beautiful.

programme.title: Angels One Five
programme.desc: Second World War drama relating the Battle of Britain through the eyes of the operations room of a Kent fighter station during the summer of 1940. A young, inexperienced pilot has trouble settling into the routine of squadron life, and his adherence to the rule book puts him out of favour with his comrades. Can he win them round?

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: The ten remaining sewers celebrate the rich fashion and textile traditions of Mexico. Host Sophie Willan and judges Patrick Grant and Esme Young are joined by a special guest judge, renowned fashion designer Erika Alvirez. In the Pattern Challenge, the sewers create a Mexican folkloric top using fabrics created by indigenous communities in Mexico’s Oaxaca region. For the Transformation Challenge, they are given manteles de hule, a traditional Mexican tablecloth. Using the stiffness of the fabric, they are asked to create a garment with an eye-catching structure. Finally, in the Made-to-Measure, the sewers design an outfit inspired by one of the many Mexican festivals found across the country.

programme.title: A Cook Abroad
programme.desc: MasterChef judge Monica Galetti steps outside her comfort zone as she swaps her chef's whites for wellies and heads for the Jura Mountains in eastern France to get hands-on with the produce she uses every day in the London restaurant where she works. Monica embarks on a road trip through one of the most beautiful yet least known regions in France, where, for the first time in her cooking career, she spends time with producers. She sees for herself how their passion translates into world-class ingredients. Immersing herself in a traditional way of life, she joins a boar hunt and faces up to the responsibility of eating meat. From beauty contests for cows to cutting down trees, she unlocks the secret to making some of our favourite French cheeses and discovers an ancient profession she never knew existed. Finally, on the slopes of Mont d'Or, Monica cooks up a rustic feast using ingredients she's gathered herself, fulfilling a personal ambition to live off the land.

programme.title: Summer Holiday
programme.desc: Don and his friends persuade their employer to lend them a London bus for their summer holiday. En route to the south of France, the boys run into some girls and offer them a lift to Athens. Then, they pick up an American boy who isn't exactly what he seems but who is running away from an exploitative mother.

programme.title: Fake or Fortune?
programme.desc: Our art sleuths investigate 15 prints found in a garage, each potentially worth thousands. Are they really by notorious 20th-century artist Lucian Freud? Or just crafty fakes?

programme.title: Evolution
programme.desc: How did the dolphin get so smart? Chris Packham dives into one of the biggest questions in nature - how intelligence itself evolved and how it arose in the extraordinary mind of the dolphin. Inside each one lies the result of a three-billion-year journey, from light-sensing cells to conscious thought.

programme.title: Superman II
programme.desc: Three Kryptonian criminals who share Superman’s extraordinary powers arrive on Earth with the intent of conquering it. Superman must use all his strength and intelligence to outwit them.

programme.title: BBC Proms
programme.desc: Nick Mohammed journeys through the Proms archive to celebrate the music that transformed people's view of the universe. Featuring Richard Strauss's Also sprach Zarathustra from 2001: A Space Odyssey, Gustav Holst's The Planets, John Williams's scores for Star Wars and E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, Hans Zimmer's Interstellar and Max Richter's On the Nature of Daylight, heard in Arrival. Prepare for a journey from the concert hall to galaxies far, far away.

programme.title: Paul Heaton at the BBC
programme.desc: One of Britain’s most prolific and successful singer-songwriters of the past four decades, Paul Heaton started his career as frontman of The Housemartins before forming The Beautiful South, the band of whom it was famously once claimed that one in seven UK households owns an album. Whether that's true or not, what is a fact is that Paul has demonstrated over the years a unique ability to write songs and lyrics that have fans weeping one moment and smiling the next. This collection of performances and best BBC moments celebrates Paul’s impressive career - the bands, the collaborations and the solo work - and features the man himself explaining the context and backstories behind some of his best-loved hits. From The Housemartins’ debut release Sheep through to Fish 'N' Chip Supper from his solo album The Mighty Several and a triumphant appearance at Glastonbury 2024 that featured a glorious reunion with Norman ‘Fatboy Slim’ Cook, it’s a celebration that can definitely guarantee viewers a Happy Hour (and a half).

programme.title: Paul Heaton: Live at Bramall Lane
programme.desc: Paul Heaton takes to the stage at Sheffield's iconic Bramall Lane for a landmark concert. Recorded live in 2025, this unforgettable performance showcases one of Britain's most admired songwriters with songs spanning more than four decades, from the timeless classics of The Housemartins and The Beautiful South to highlights from his solo career. Backed by his stellar live band, including regular singing partner Rianne Downey, Paul Heaton delivers a set filled with wit, warmth and unmistakable melodies, performing beloved favourites alongside newer material for an audience at his beloved Sheffield United Football Club.

programme.title: The Housemartins in London 0 Hull 4
programme.desc: The Housemartins wake up one morning to discover that suddenly they're the fourth-best band in Hull. This intimate documentary is a unique record of the early days, looking at how a meteoric rise to fame left their home lives irrevocably unchanged. First broadcast 1987.

programme.title: Top of the Pops
programme.desc: A compilation of Top of the Pops performances from The Beautiful South.

programme.desc: It’s all change at Hawx Academy as former Foxborough player Charlie must prove herself to her teammates, their new coach and an all-access documentary crew.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Frances Tophill returns to Damson Farm in Bath and spends the day with owner Alison and a very special guest – Dame Mary Berry. Returning to the city where she grew up and went to school, Mary shares how the landscapes and countryside around Bath nurtured a lifelong love of gardening and the great outdoors. Together, they share practical gardening advice and celebrate the very best of summer, harvesting homegrown fruit, vegetables and flowers at their seasonal peak. Frances has advice on how to create a wild corner that's both beautiful and beneficial for wildlife while collecting seeds for future displays. Arit Anderson visits an inspiring urban edible garden in London, and there's a city gardener transforming a compact space into a thriving haven for wildlife. Toby Buckland shares clever ways to extend the growing season and make the most of summer harvests, and in Birmingham, there's a visit to a predominantly Punjabi allotment community where growing exceptional produce is intertwined with family, culture and tradition, creating plots that are as productive as they are beautiful.

programme.title: Angels One Five
programme.desc: Second World War drama relating the Battle of Britain through the eyes of the operations room of a Kent fighter station during the summer of 1940. A young, inexperienced pilot has trouble settling into the routine of squadron life, and his adherence to the rule book puts him out of favour with his comrades. Can he win them round?

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: The ten remaining sewers celebrate the rich fashion and textile traditions of Mexico. Host Sophie Willan and judges Patrick Grant and Esme Young are joined by a special guest judge, renowned fashion designer Erika Alvirez. In the Pattern Challenge, the sewers create a Mexican folkloric top using fabrics created by indigenous communities in Mexico’s Oaxaca region. For the Transformation Challenge, they are given manteles de hule, a traditional Mexican tablecloth. Using the stiffness of the fabric, they are asked to create a garment with an eye-catching structure. Finally, in the Made-to-Measure, the sewers design an outfit inspired by one of the many Mexican festivals found across the country.

programme.title: A Cook Abroad
programme.desc: MasterChef judge Monica Galetti steps outside her comfort zone as she swaps her chef's whites for wellies and heads for the Jura Mountains in eastern France to get hands-on with the produce she uses every day in the London restaurant where she works. Monica embarks on a road trip through one of the most beautiful yet least known regions in France, where, for the first time in her cooking career, she spends time with producers. She sees for herself how their passion translates into world-class ingredients. Immersing herself in a traditional way of life, she joins a boar hunt and faces up to the responsibility of eating meat. From beauty contests for cows to cutting down trees, she unlocks the secret to making some of our favourite French cheeses and discovers an ancient profession she never knew existed. Finally, on the slopes of Mont d'Or, Monica cooks up a rustic feast using ingredients she's gathered herself, fulfilling a personal ambition to live off the land.

programme.title: Summer Holiday
programme.desc: Don and his friends persuade their employer to lend them a London bus for their summer holiday. En route to the south of France, the boys run into some girls and offer them a lift to Athens. Then, they pick up an American boy who isn't exactly what he seems but who is running away from an exploitative mother.

programme.title: Fake or Fortune?
programme.desc: Our art sleuths investigate 15 prints found in a garage, each potentially worth thousands. Are they really by notorious 20th-century artist Lucian Freud? Or just crafty fakes?

programme.title: Evolution
programme.desc: How did the dolphin get so smart? Chris Packham dives into one of the biggest questions in nature - how intelligence itself evolved and how it arose in the extraordinary mind of the dolphin. Inside each one lies the result of a three-billion-year journey, from light-sensing cells to conscious thought.

programme.title: Superman II
programme.desc: Three Kryptonian criminals who share Superman’s extraordinary powers arrive on Earth with the intent of conquering it. Superman must use all his strength and intelligence to outwit them.

programme.title: BBC Proms
programme.desc: Nick Mohammed journeys through the Proms archive to celebrate the music that transformed people's view of the universe. Featuring Richard Strauss's Also sprach Zarathustra from 2001: A Space Odyssey, Gustav Holst's The Planets, John Williams's scores for Star Wars and E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, Hans Zimmer's Interstellar and Max Richter's On the Nature of Daylight, heard in Arrival. Prepare for a journey from the concert hall to galaxies far, far away.

programme.title: Paul Heaton at the BBC
programme.desc: One of Britain’s most prolific and successful singer-songwriters of the past four decades, Paul Heaton started his career as frontman of The Housemartins before forming The Beautiful South, the band of whom it was famously once claimed that one in seven UK households owns an album. Whether that's true or not, what is a fact is that Paul has demonstrated over the years a unique ability to write songs and lyrics that have fans weeping one moment and smiling the next. This collection of performances and best BBC moments celebrates Paul’s impressive career - the bands, the collaborations and the solo work - and features the man himself explaining the context and backstories behind some of his best-loved hits. From The Housemartins’ debut release Sheep through to Fish 'N' Chip Supper from his solo album The Mighty Several and a triumphant appearance at Glastonbury 2024 that featured a glorious reunion with Norman ‘Fatboy Slim’ Cook, it’s a celebration that can definitely guarantee viewers a Happy Hour (and a half).

programme.title: Paul Heaton: Live at Bramall Lane
programme.desc: Paul Heaton takes to the stage at Sheffield's iconic Bramall Lane for a landmark concert. Recorded live in 2025, this unforgettable performance showcases one of Britain's most admired songwriters with songs spanning more than four decades, from the timeless classics of The Housemartins and The Beautiful South to highlights from his solo career. Backed by his stellar live band, including regular singing partner Rianne Downey, Paul Heaton delivers a set filled with wit, warmth and unmistakable melodies, performing beloved favourites alongside newer material for an audience at his beloved Sheffield United Football Club.

programme.title: The Housemartins in London 0 Hull 4
programme.desc: The Housemartins wake up one morning to discover that suddenly they're the fourth-best band in Hull. This intimate documentary is a unique record of the early days, looking at how a meteoric rise to fame left their home lives irrevocably unchanged. First broadcast 1987.

Aki Kaurismäki's Nordic comedy romance, winner of the Cannes Festival Jury Prize. In Finnish with English subtitles.

programme.title: Force Of Nature
programme.desc: Documentary series revealing the incredible ways in which all life is impacted by our journey around the Sun. As the planet’s shifting rain patterns rewrite the rules, survival is no longer about strength alone - it is about timing, instinct, and the courage to move forwards when faced with rising flood waters. From the desert to the jungle, three mothers face the ultimate test of survival - monsoon floodwaters tear through pygmy elephant territory in the rainforests of Borneo as a mother must lead her calf across a raging river to get to higher ground, and a female platypus in Australia watches a flash flood destroy her home river in a single day. With breeding season looming, the platypus abandons her home and ventures into the human world on a desperate journey to find a new river in time to lay her eggs - elsewhere, a flood in the middle of the desert in Africa brings bountiful prey for a lone lioness raising eight cubs who uses sand and water to trap buffalo five times her size.

programme.title: Long Lost Family
programme.desc: Our first case of this episode concerns Jayne - every year on Bonfire Night, her late mother retreated from the family festivities. When she reemerged, the family always knew she'd been crying and Jayne later found out why: when her mum was 20 and unmarried, she'd had a son who was placed for adoption. While Jayne wants to find her older brother to tell him he was always thought of and loved, Kevin and his late wife had a baby girl together when they were just teenagers and, at their parents' insistence, put her up for adoption - the couple stayed together and had more children, but they never forgot their eldest daughter and Kevin is determined to find her.

programme.title: Prue Leith's Cotswold Kitchen
programme.desc: This series takes us into the home of Prue Leith and her husband John as she, friends and her husband cook mouth-watering dishes and explore the joys of their Cotswold home and local area. In this episode, Prue welcomes her good friend Sandi Toksvig into her Cotswold Kitchen - history buff Sandi cooks two dishes from the 1920s that were printed in pamphlets put together by women across the country to fundraise. The first dish is a ham and egg pie written by Enid Blyton followed by meatless sausage, but the instructions and measurements are rather vague and could result in disaster. Prue also makes a vegan dish that was her late brother's favourite, and her husband John joins her in the kitchen to make his signature homemade yoghurt - Prue then shows how yoghurt can be transformed from a breakfast staple into a dinner party desert, there's a handy hack for cooking the perfect steak, and John heads outside with Philippa the gardener to make a stunning countryside wreath.

programme.title: Sorry, I Didn't Know
programme.desc: Chizzy Akudolu hosts the classic panel show with a twist as four fantastically funny guests join team leaders Richard Blackwood and Eddie Kadi to take viewers on a tour of Black British history - this time it's Desiree Burch, Ria Hebden, Matt Richardson and Shazia Mirza joining the team leaders. Insightful, educational, bold, tongue-in-cheek and above all very funny, the teams will battle over four rounds - from guessing why unknown faces from history should be famous to uncovering a treasure trove of facts about Africa, this show educates as much as it entertains with a fabulous array of comedians from all backgrounds. It's history with a touch of colour...

programme.title: Force Of Nature
programme.desc: Documentary series revealing the incredible ways in which all life is impacted by our journey around the Sun. As the planet’s shifting rain patterns rewrite the rules, survival is no longer about strength alone - it is about timing, instinct, and the courage to move forwards when faced with rising flood waters. From the desert to the jungle, three mothers face the ultimate test of survival - monsoon floodwaters tear through pygmy elephant territory in the rainforests of Borneo as a mother must lead her calf across a raging river to get to higher ground, and a female platypus in Australia watches a flash flood destroy her home river in a single day. With breeding season looming, the platypus abandons her home and ventures into the human world on a desperate journey to find a new river in time to lay her eggs - elsewhere, a flood in the middle of the desert in Africa brings bountiful prey for a lone lioness raising eight cubs who uses sand and water to trap buffalo five times her size.

programme.title: Long Lost Family
programme.desc: Our first case of this episode concerns Jayne - every year on Bonfire Night, her late mother retreated from the family festivities. When she reemerged, the family always knew she'd been crying and Jayne later found out why: when her mum was 20 and unmarried, she'd had a son who was placed for adoption. While Jayne wants to find her older brother to tell him he was always thought of and loved, Kevin and his late wife had a baby girl together when they were just teenagers and, at their parents' insistence, put her up for adoption - the couple stayed together and had more children, but they never forgot their eldest daughter and Kevin is determined to find her.

programme.title: Quantum of Solace
programme.desc: The 22nd entry in the James Bond film franchise. Is there solace in revenge? 007 and M track a shadowy international network of power and corruption reaping billions - as James pursues the agents of an assassination attempt on M, all roads lead to Dominic Greene, a world-renowned developer of green technology. Greene is intent on securing a barren area of Bolivia in exchange for helping a strongman stage a coup there - as the CIA looks the other way, only Bond stands against him...

programme.title: The Staircase
programme.desc: In 2003, tensions rise and old wounds reopen as the Petersons' eldest son Clayton returns home and unwittingly makes a critical discovery. programme.title: Sorry, I Didn't Know
programme.desc: Chizzy Akudolu hosts the classic panel show with a twist as four fantastically funny guests join team leaders Richard Blackwood and Eddie Kadi to take viewers on a tour of Black British history - this time it's Desiree Burch, Ria Hebden, Matt Richardson and Shazia Mirza joining the team leaders. Insightful, educational, bold, tongue-in-cheek and above all very funny, the teams will battle over four rounds - from guessing why unknown faces from history should be famous to uncovering a treasure trove of facts about Africa, this show educates as much as it entertains with a fabulous array of comedians from all backgrounds. It's history with a touch of colour...

programme.title: Force Of Nature
programme.desc: Documentary series revealing the incredible ways in which all life is impacted by our journey around the Sun. As the planet’s shifting rain patterns rewrite the rules, survival is no longer about strength alone - it is about timing, instinct, and the courage to move forwards when faced with rising flood waters. From the desert to the jungle, three mothers face the ultimate test of survival - monsoon floodwaters tear through pygmy elephant territory in the rainforests of Borneo as a mother must lead her calf across a raging river to get to higher ground, and a female platypus in Australia watches a flash flood destroy her home river in a single day. With breeding season looming, the platypus abandons her home and ventures into the human world on a desperate journey to find a new river in time to lay her eggs - elsewhere, a flood in the middle of the desert in Africa brings bountiful prey for a lone lioness raising eight cubs who uses sand and water to trap buffalo five times her size.

programme.title: Long Lost Family
programme.desc: Our first case of this episode concerns Jayne - every year on Bonfire Night, her late mother retreated from the family festivities. When she reemerged, the family always knew she'd been crying and Jayne later found out why: when her mum was 20 and unmarried, she'd had a son who was placed for adoption. While Jayne wants to find her older brother to tell him he was always thought of and loved, Kevin and his late wife had a baby girl together when they were just teenagers and, at their parents' insistence, put her up for adoption - the couple stayed together and had more children, but they never forgot their eldest daughter and Kevin is determined to find her.

programme.title: Prue Leith's Cotswold Kitchen
programme.desc: This series takes us into the home of Prue Leith and her husband John as she, friends and her husband cook mouth-watering dishes and explore the joys of their Cotswold home and local area. In this episode, Prue welcomes her good friend Sandi Toksvig into her Cotswold Kitchen - history buff Sandi cooks two dishes from the 1920s that were printed in pamphlets put together by women across the country to fundraise. The first dish is a ham and egg pie written by Enid Blyton followed by meatless sausage, but the instructions and measurements are rather vague and could result in disaster. Prue also makes a vegan dish that was her late brother's favourite, and her husband John joins her in the kitchen to make his signature homemade yoghurt - Prue then shows how yoghurt can be transformed from a breakfast staple into a dinner party desert, there's a handy hack for cooking the perfect steak, and John heads outside with Philippa the gardener to make a stunning countryside wreath.

From the desert to the jungle, three mothers face the ultimate test of survival - monsoon floodwaters tear through pygmy elephant territory in the rainforests of Borneo as a mother must lead her calf across a raging river to get to higher ground, and a female platypus in Australia watches a flash flood destroy her home river in a single day. With breeding season looming, the platypus abandons her home and ventures into the human world on a desperate journey to find a new river in time to lay her eggs - elsewhere, a flood in the middle of the desert in Africa brings bountiful prey for a lone lioness raising eight cubs who uses sand and water to trap buffalo five times her size.

programme.title: Long Lost Family
programme.desc: Our first case of this episode concerns Jayne - every year on Bonfire Night, her late mother retreated from the family festivities. When she reemerged, the family always knew she'd been crying and Jayne later found out why: when her mum was 20 and unmarried, she'd had a son who was placed for adoption. While Jayne wants to find her older brother to tell him he was always thought of and loved, Kevin and his late wife had a baby girl together when they were just teenagers and, at their parents' insistence, put her up for adoption - the couple stayed together and had more children, but they never forgot their eldest daughter and Kevin is determined to find her.

programme.title: Prue Leith's Cotswold Kitchen
programme.desc: This series takes us into the home of Prue Leith and her husband John as she, friends and her husband cook mouth-watering dishes and explore the joys of their Cotswold home and local area. In this episode, Prue welcomes her good friend Sandi Toksvig into her Cotswold Kitchen - history buff Sandi cooks two dishes from the 1920s that were printed in pamphlets put together by women across the country to fundraise. The first dish is a ham and egg pie written by Enid Blyton followed by meatless sausage, but the instructions and measurements are rather vague and could result in disaster. Prue also makes a vegan dish that was her late brother's favourite, and her husband John joins her in the kitchen to make his signature homemade yoghurt - Prue then shows how yoghurt can be transformed from a breakfast staple into a dinner party desert, there's a handy hack for cooking the perfect steak, and John heads outside with Philippa the gardener to make a stunning countryside wreath.

programme.title: Sorry, I Didn't Know
programme.desc: Chizzy Akudolu hosts the classic panel show with a twist as four fantastically funny guests join team leaders Richard Blackwood and Eddie Kadi to take viewers on a tour of Black British history - this time it's Desiree Burch, Ria Hebden, Matt Richardson and Shazia Mirza joining the team leaders. Insightful, educational, bold, tongue-in-cheek and above all very funny, the teams will battle over four rounds - from guessing why unknown faces from history should be famous to uncovering a treasure trove of facts about Africa, this show educates as much as it entertains with a fabulous array of comedians from all backgrounds. It's history with a touch of colour...

programme.title: Sorry, I Didn't Know
programme.desc: Chizzy Akudolu hosts the classic panel show with a twist as four fantastically funny guests join team leaders Richard Blackwood and Eddie Kadi to take viewers on a tour of Black British history - this time it's Desiree Burch, Ria Hebden, Matt Richardson and Shazia Mirza joining the team leaders. Insightful, educational, bold, tongue-in-cheek and above all very funny, the teams will battle over four rounds - from guessing why unknown faces from history should be famous to uncovering a treasure trove of facts about Africa, this show educates as much as it entertains with a fabulous array of comedians from all backgrounds. programme.title: Force Of Nature
programme.desc: Documentary series revealing the incredible ways in which all life is impacted by our journey around the Sun. As the planet’s shifting rain patterns rewrite the rules, survival is no longer about strength alone - it is about timing, instinct, and the courage to move forwards when faced with rising flood waters. From the desert to the jungle, three mothers face the ultimate test of survival - monsoon floodwaters tear through pygmy elephant territory in the rainforests of Borneo as a mother must lead her calf across a raging river to get to higher ground, and a female platypus in Australia watches a flash flood destroy her home river in a single day. With breeding season looming, the platypus abandons her home and ventures into the human world on a desperate journey to find a new river in time to lay her eggs - elsewhere, a flood in the middle of the desert in Africa brings bountiful prey for a lone lioness raising eight cubs who uses sand and water to trap buffalo five times her size.

programme.title: Long Lost Family
programme.desc: Our first case of this episode concerns Jayne - every year on Bonfire Night, her late mother retreated from the family festivities. When she reemerged, the family always knew she'd been crying and Jayne later found out why: when her mum was 20 and unmarried, she'd had a son who was placed for adoption. While Jayne wants to find her older brother to tell him he was always thought of and loved, Kevin and his late wife had a baby girl together when they were just teenagers and, at their parents' insistence, put her up for adoption - the couple stayed together and had more children, but they never forgot their eldest daughter and Kevin is determined to find her.

programme.title: Prue Leith's Cotswold Kitchen
programme.desc: This series takes us into the home of Prue Leith and her husband John as she, friends and her husband cook mouth-watering dishes and explore the joys of their Cotswold home and local area. In this episode, Prue welcomes her good friend Sandi Toksvig into her Cotswold Kitchen - history buff Sandi cooks two dishes from the 1920s that were printed in pamphlets put together by women across the country to fundraise. The first dish is a ham and egg pie written by Enid Blyton followed by meatless sausage, but the instructions and measurements are rather vague and could result in disaster. Prue also makes a vegan dish that was her late brother's favourite, and her husband John joins her in the kitchen to make his signature homemade yoghurt - Prue then shows how yoghurt can be transformed from a breakfast staple into a dinner party desert, there's a handy hack for cooking the perfect steak, and John heads outside with Philippa the gardener to make a stunning countryside wreath.

programme.title: Sorry, I Didn't Know
programme.desc: Chizzy Akudolu hosts the classic panel show with a twist as four fantastically funny guests join team leaders Richard Blackwood and Eddie Kadi to take viewers on a tour of Black British history - this time it's Desiree Burch, Ria Hebden, Matt Richardson and Shazia Mirza joining the team leaders. Insightful, educational, bold, tongue-in-cheek and above all very funny, the teams will battle over four rounds - from guessing why unknown faces from history should be famous to uncovering a treasure trove of facts about Africa, this show educates as much as it entertains with a fabulous array of comedians from all backgrounds. It's history with a touch of colour...

programme.title: Force Of Nature
programme.desc: Documentary series revealing the incredible ways in which all life is impacted by our journey around the Sun. As the planet’s shifting rain patterns rewrite the rules, survival is no longer about strength alone - it is about timing, instinct, and the courage to move forwards when faced with rising flood waters. From the desert to the jungle, three mothers face the ultimate test of survival - monsoon floodwaters tear through pygmy elephant territory in the rainforests of Borneo as a mother must lead her calf across a raging river to get to higher ground, and a female platypus in Australia watches a flash flood destroy her home river in a single day. With breeding season looming, the platypus abandons her home and ventures into the human world on a desperate journey to find a new river in time to lay her eggs - elsewhere, a flood in the middle of the desert in Africa brings bountiful prey for a lone lioness raising eight cubs who uses sand and water to trap buffalo five times her size.

programme.title: Long Lost Family
programme.desc: Our first case of this episode concerns Jayne - every year on Bonfire Night, her late mother retreated from the family festivities. When she reemerged, the family always knew she'd been crying and Jayne later found out why: when her mum was 20 and unmarried, she'd had a son who was placed for adoption. While Jayne wants to find her older brother to tell him he was always thought of and loved, Kevin and his late wife had a baby girl together when they were just teenagers and, at their parents' insistence, put her up for adoption - the couple stayed together and had more children, but they never forgot their eldest daughter and Kevin is determined to find her.

programme.title: Prue Leith's Cotswold Kitchen
programme.desc: This series takes us into the home of Prue Leith and her husband John as she, friends and her husband cook mouth-watering dishes and explore the joys of their Cotswold home and local area. In this episode, Prue welcomes her good friend Sandi Toksvig into her Cotswold Kitchen - history buff Sandi cooks two dishes from the 1920s that were printed in pamphlets put together by women across the country to fundraise. The first dish is a ham and egg pie written by Enid Blyton followed by meatless sausage, but the instructions and measurements are rather vague and could result in disaster. Prue also makes a vegan dish that was her late brother's favourite, and her husband John joins her in the kitchen to make his signature homemade yoghurt - Prue then shows how yoghurt can be transformed from a breakfast staple into a dinner party desert, there's a handy hack for cooking the perfect steak, and John heads outside with Philippa the gardener to make a stunning countryside wreath.

programme.title: Sorry, I Didn't Know
programme.desc: Chizzy Akudolu hosts the classic panel show with a twist as four fantastically funny guests join team leaders Richard Blackwood and Eddie Kadi to take viewers on a tour of Black British history - this time it's Desiree Burch, Ria Hebden, Matt Richardson and Shazia Mirza joining the team leaders. Insightful, educational, bold, tongue-in-cheek and above all very funny, the teams will battle over four rounds - from guessing why unknown faces from history should be famous to uncovering a treasure trove of facts about Africa, this show educates as much as it entertains with a fabulous array of comedians from all backgrounds. programme.title: Force Of Nature
programme.desc: Documentary series revealing the incredible ways in which all life is impacted by our journey around the Sun. As the planet’s shifting rain patterns rewrite the rules, survival is no longer about strength alone - it is about timing, instinct, and the courage to move forwards when faced with rising flood waters. From the desert to the jungle, three mothers face the ultimate test of survival - monsoon floodwaters tear through pygmy elephant territory in the rainforests of Borneo as a mother must lead her calf across a raging river to get to higher ground, and a female platypus in Australia watches a flash flood destroy her home river in a single day. With breeding season looming, the platypus abandons her home and ventures into the human world on a desperate journey to find a new river in time to lay her eggs - elsewhere, a flood in the middle of the desert in Africa brings bountiful prey for a lone lioness raising eight cubs who uses sand and water to trap buffalo five times her size.

programme.title: Long Lost Family
programme.desc: Our first case of this episode concerns Jayne - every year on Bonfire Night, her late mother retreated from the family festivities. When she reemerged, the family always knew she'd been crying and Jayne later found out why: when her mum was 20 and unmarried, she'd had a son who was placed for adoption. While Jayne wants to find her older brother to tell him he was always thought of and loved, Kevin and his late wife had a baby girl together when they were just teenagers and, at their parents' insistence, put her up for adoption - the couple stayed together and had more children, but they never forgot their eldest daughter and Kevin is determined to find her.

programme.title: Prue Leith's Cotswold Kitchen
programme.desc: This series takes us into the home of Prue Leith and her husband John as she, friends and her husband cook mouth-watering dishes and explore the joys of their Cotswold home and local area. In this episode, Prue welcomes her good friend Sandi Toksvig into her Cotswold Kitchen - history buff Sandi cooks two dishes from the 1920s that were printed in pamphlets put together by women across the country to fundraise. The first dish is a ham and egg pie written by Enid Blyton followed by meatless sausage, but the instructions and measurements are rather vague and could result in disaster. Prue also makes a vegan dish that was her late brother's favourite, and her husband John joins her in the kitchen to make his signature homemade yoghurt - Prue then shows how yoghurt can be transformed from a breakfast staple into a dinner party desert, there's a handy hack for cooking the perfect steak, and John heads outside with Philippa the gardener to make a stunning countryside wreath.

programme.title: Sorry, I Didn't Know
programme.desc: Chizzy Akudolu hosts the classic panel show with a twist as four fantastically funny guests join team leaders Richard Blackwood and Eddie Kadi to take viewers on a tour of Black British history - this time it's Desiree Burch, Ria Hebden, Matt Richardson and Shazia Mirza joining the team leaders. Insightful, educational, bold, tongue-in-cheek and above all very funny, the teams will battle over four rounds - from guessing why unknown faces from history should be famous to uncovering a treasure trove of facts about Africa, this show educates as much as it entertains with a fabulous array of comedians from all backgrounds. It's history with a touch of colour...

programme.title: Force Of Nature
programme.desc: Documentary series revealing the incredible ways in which all life is impacted by our journey around the Sun. As the planet’s shifting rain patterns rewrite the rules, survival is no longer about strength alone - it is about timing, instinct, and the courage to move forwards when faced with rising flood waters. From the desert to the jungle, three mothers face the ultimate test of survival - monsoon floodwaters tear through pygmy elephant territory in the rainforests of Borneo as a mother must lead her calf across a raging river to get to higher ground, and a female platypus in Australia watches a flash flood destroy her home river in a single day. With breeding season looming, the platypus abandons her home and ventures into the human world on a desperate journey to find a new river in time to lay her eggs - elsewhere, a flood in the middle of the desert in Africa brings bountiful prey for a lone lioness raising eight cubs who uses sand and water to trap buffalo five times her size.

programme.title: Long Lost Family
programme.desc: Our first case of this episode concerns Jayne - every year on Bonfire Night, her late mother retreated from the family festivities. When she reemerged, the family always knew she'd been crying and Jayne later found out why: when her mum was 20 and unmarried, she'd had a son who was placed for adoption. While Jayne wants to find her older brother to tell him he was always thought of and loved, Kevin and his late wife had a baby girl together when they were just teenagers and, at their parents' insistence, put her up for adoption - the couple stayed together and had more children, but they never forgot their eldest daughter and Kevin is determined to find her.

programme.title: Prue Leith's Cotswold Kitchen
programme.desc: This series takes us into the home of Prue Leith and her husband John as she, friends and her husband cook mouth-watering dishes and explore the joys of their Cotswold home and local area. In this episode, Prue welcomes her good friend Sandi Toksvig into her Cotswold Kitchen - history buff Sandi cooks two dishes from the 1920s that were printed in pamphlets put together by women across the country to fundraise. The first dish is a ham and egg pie written by Enid Blyton followed by meatless sausage, but the instructions and measurements are rather vague and could result in disaster. Prue also makes a vegan dish that was her late brother's favourite, and her husband John joins her in the kitchen to make his signature homemade yoghurt - Prue then shows how yoghurt can be transformed from a breakfast staple into a dinner party desert, there's a handy hack for cooking the perfect steak, and John heads outside with Philippa the gardener to make a stunning countryside wreath.

programme.title: Force Of Nature
programme.desc: Documentary series revealing the incredible ways in which all life is impacted by our journey around the Sun. As the planet’s shifting rain patterns rewrite the rules, survival is no longer about strength alone - it is about timing, instinct, and the courage to move forwards when faced with rising flood waters. From the desert to the jungle, three mothers face the ultimate test of survival - monsoon floodwaters tear through pygmy elephant territory in the rainforests of Borneo as a mother must lead her calf across a raging river to get to higher ground, and a female platypus in Australia watches a flash flood destroy her home river in a single day. With breeding season looming, the platypus abandons her home and ventures into the human world on a desperate journey to find a new river in time to lay her eggs - elsewhere, a flood in the middle of the desert in Africa brings bountiful prey for a lone lioness raising eight cubs who uses sand and water to trap buffalo five times her size.

programme.title: Long Lost Family
programme.desc: Our first case of this episode concerns Jayne - every year on Bonfire Night, her late mother retreated from the family festivities. When she reemerged, the family always knew she'd been crying and Jayne later found out why: when her mum was 20 and unmarried, she'd had a son who was placed for adoption. While Jayne wants to find her older brother to tell him he was always thought of and loved, Kevin and his late wife had a baby girl together when they were just teenagers and, at their parents' insistence, put her up for adoption - the couple stayed together and had more children, but they never forgot their eldest daughter and Kevin is determined to find her.

programme.desc: On a dark night in the village of March Magna, Barnaby's wife Joyce swerves her car to narrowly miss a shadowy figure in the road... or so she thinks.
