programme.title: Midsomer Murders
programme.desc: Piano student Zoe Stock has won a place at the Devington Manor Winter School led by internationally renowned musician Sir Michael Fielding when, from the riverbank in the grounds of the manor, she sees a woman jump from the bridge and disappear underwater - when Barnaby and Jones start investigating the possible drowning, they discover unsavoury connections to the past that could prove lethal 20 years later. Can they intervene before the body count escalates, and will the talented Zoe survive her master class?

programme.title: Midsomer Murders
programme.desc: Betrayal, infidelity and blackmail fester as plans to re-enact a Victorian prizefight turn nasty - and even DCI Barnaby finds his judgement clouded by an old friend. Midsomer Morchard prepares to welcome back local boxer John Kinsella from his world title fight victory in New York - Kinsella is returning with his ruthless and controlling promoter Frank Bishop to take part in a re-enactment of a match from 1860. When Bishop arrives, he goes to see solicitor Giles Braithwaite but instead finds the lawyer dead - meanwhile, trainer Teddy Molloy is working with another fighter called Ken Tuohy, who suspects Kinsella of a dalliance with his fiancee. There are plenty of other grudges and secrets simmering in the village, with revelations of discord, adultery, gambling and Giles's assistant Iris being accused of blackmail. When it comes time for the re-enactment, Tuohy takes the place of Kinsella's opponent and attacks Kinsella - Bishop is then found dead. Can Barnaby find the killer?

programme.title: Midsomer Murders
programme.desc: A planning dispute turns to murder after a leading light in the Midsomer Conservation Society suspects her neighbours are involved in a money-making development scam. Political wrangling, burglaries and sexual liaisons abound in picturesque Great Pelfe, but why is someone driven to start killing? As Maureen is attacked with a broken bottle in the grounds and bleeds to death, planning officer Liz Gerrard beds Rogers and police discover that the victims of a spate of burglaries and vandalism all support a controversial development at Pelfe Chase. Barnaby then finds a catapult at Maureen's house - was she the vandal? As Election Day approaches, Jones suspects that Fiona has given Norman Swascombe free land as a bung, but the truth surprises him - meanwhile, a night of passion for Liz and Otley turns deadly... As Dr Bullard discovers that Rogers was killed using Otley's veterinary drugs, Barnaby realises that the murderer will not stop until everyone who knows the truth is silenced.

programme.title: Vera
programme.desc: Detective drama series based on the novels by Ann Cleeves. Vera investigates the mysterious death of Anne-Marie Richards, whose body is discovered by a young girl on the wild and desolate Northumberland moors. Anne-Marie has recently returned from Scotland to attempt a reconciliation with her two daughters; a 999 call on the night of the murder and the disturbed state of her cottage suggest that she may have been abducted by someone she knew. The fractious relationship between the victim and her family arouses Vera's suspicions - who has been posting abusive comments about Anne-Marie online, and did she have a connection to the Newcastle businessman who has been spending time on the coast? What Vera and her team do not know is that this event will have long-term and devastating effects on all of them...

programme.title: Sharpe
programme.desc: Napoleonic War-based action-adventure. June 1813 - the South Essex is seriously short of men, and when the Duke of Wellington is told that there are no recruits available, he sends Sharpe to England to investigate. When Sharpe and Harper arrive, they are informed that there are 700 men waiting for them in Chelmsford - however, Sharpe finds the barracks deserted with no sign of his missing regiment. He and Harper decide to assume other identities and enlist - recruited by Sergeant Havercamp, Sharpe and Harper arrive at a training camp near the estate of Sir Henry Simmerson where they are trained mercilessly. Sharpe discovers that the new recruits are being auctioned to other regiments and returns to the Horse Guards with this information to entrust it to an old friend called Lawford... but Lawford wants to avoid a scandal and promptly tells Lord Fenner, who tries to have Sharpe killed. With the help of Fenner's mistress Lady Anne, Sharpe must now find the proof to implicate Fenner.

programme.title: Sharpe
programme.desc: Napoleonic War-based action-adventure. Winter 1813 - Wellington is informed by the debonair Comte de Maquerre that Bordeaux is ready to rebel against Napoleon, but Wellington's spymaster Ross is suspicious and tests Maquerre by suggesting that they use Maquerre's own castle as a base. Maquerre reluctantly agrees but says that the castle is in Napoleon's hands, so Wellington appoints Colonel Bampfylde to lead the attack on the castle with Sharpe in support. Bampfylde, who is intent on glory, sends Sharpe on a scouting mission and tries to capture the castle on his own, but he fails and casualties are heavy - Sharpe, who is a witness to the carnage, therefore has Harris and Frederickson sneak into the castle in disguise, and they soon force the French to surrender once inside. Ashamed by Sharpe's victory, Bampfylde sends him off on a reconnaissance mission - however, Sharpe soon discovers that Bordeaux has no intention of rising against Napoleon and that Maquerre is a double agent.

programme.title: Force Of Nature
programme.desc: Documentary series revealing the incredible ways in which all life is impacted by our journey around the Sun. As the planet’s shifting rain patterns rewrite the rules, survival is no longer about strength alone - it is about timing, instinct, and the courage to move forwards when faced with rising flood waters. From the desert to the jungle, three mothers face the ultimate test of survival - monsoon floodwaters tear through pygmy elephant territory in the rainforests of Borneo as a mother must lead her calf across a raging river to get to higher ground, and a female platypus in Australia watches a flash flood destroy her home river in a single day. With breeding season looming, the platypus abandons her home and ventures into the human world on a desperate journey to find a new river in time to lay her eggs - elsewhere, a flood in the middle of the desert in Africa brings bountiful prey for a lone lioness raising eight cubs who uses sand and water to trap buffalo five times her size.

programme.title: Long Lost Family
programme.desc: Our first case of this episode concerns Jayne - every year on Bonfire Night, her late mother retreated from the family festivities. When she reemerged, the family always knew she'd been crying and Jayne later found out why: when her mum was 20 and unmarried, she'd had a son who was placed for adoption. While Jayne wants to find her older brother to tell him he was always thought of and loved, Kevin and his late wife had a baby girl together when they were just teenagers and, at their parents' insistence, put her up for adoption - the couple stayed together and had more children, but they never forgot their eldest daughter and Kevin is determined to find her.

In this episode, Prue welcomes her good friend Sandi Toksvig into her Cotswold Kitchen - history buff Sandi cooks two dishes from the 1920s that were printed in pamphlets put together by women across the country to fundraise. The first dish is a ham and egg pie written by Enid Blyton followed by meatless sausage, but the instructions and measurements are rather vague and could result in disaster. Prue also makes a vegan dish that was her late brother's favourite, and her husband John joins her in the kitchen to make his signature homemade yoghurt - Prue then shows how yoghurt can be transformed from a breakfast staple into a dinner party desert, there's a handy hack for cooking the perfect steak, and John heads outside with Philippa the gardener to make a stunning countryside wreath.
